findings.evidence: The text infers f^n = gh from D(g) subset D(f) and g in sqrt((f)); the latter gives g^n = fh instead. In k[x,y], f=x and g=xy give D(g) subset D(f), but x^n=xyh has no solution h in k[x,y]. The restriction map can be justified with the corrected relation, but this displayed inference is false. Assigned consumer: def-associated-sheaf-graded-module-proj.

The proof establishes equality on one selected intersection D(f_i f_{i_j}), then invokes the finite-cover uniqueness step on D(f_i)=D(f_i) union D(f_i f_{i_j}). This cover includes all of D(f_i) as one member, where vanishing has not been established, so the uniqueness hypothesis does not apply. It needs equality over all intersections with the finite subcover. Assigned consumers: def-associated-sheaf-graded-module-proj and thm-serre-criterion-ampleness.
